quality_notes: This is a recent peer-reviewed publication, but the farm production survey refers to the 2021/22 season; do not describe the unit costs as current 2026 prices.
The 50-farmer survey covers two provinces in the Saïss plain and should not be generalized to all Morocco.
The itemized costs are presented in the paper's working-capital budget for a supplemental-irrigation programme, not necessarily audited average farmer expenditure.
The paper reports grain yields from 4 to 50 quintals/ha across farms; retain the range and context rather than using its upper bound as a default yield.

The study is useful for a wheat enterprise budget structure and local production coefficients, but current seed, fertilizer, labour, machinery and irrigation tariffs still require dated invoices or official price schedules.

For Saïss wheat, obtain current 2026/27 invoices and farmer accounts to update the 2021/22 survey coefficients and programme-budget unit costs; separately validate irrigated and rainfed production systems.
conclusion: Morocco remains research-only. The evidence base now includes a 50-farmer Saïss wheat survey (production practices and 2021/22 yields) plus partial itemized costs from a supplemental-irrigation programme budget; historical Souss-Massa greenhouse tomato producer interviews; an INRA-affiliated tomato farm-survey methodology; October 2026 sector-reported tomato cost/yield stress; and the 2026 soft-wheat campaign reference terms. The wheat cost lines are useful historical regional benchmarks, not current national costs. No crop has a complete, current, nationally representative budget and no calculator data are activated.
